title: Sparsified Preconditioned Conjugate Gradient Solver on GPUs
problem: Preconditioned iterative sparse linear solvers have data dependences between iterations that limit parallelization, especially problematic for GPUs with many parallel cores.
motivation: Overcome parallelization limitations in preconditioned solvers by reducing interdependencies while maintaining convergence behavior.
method: Propose sparsified preconditioned conjugate gradient (SPCG) solver that increases parallelism through sparsification of the preconditioner. Reduces iteration dependences while preserving convergence. Evaluated with ILU(0) and ILU(K) preconditioners on symmetric positive definite (SPD) matrices.
key_novelty: Sparsification technique for preconditioners to increase parallelism in iterative solvers on GPUs without sacrificing convergence properties.
contributions: Sparsified preconditioned conjugate gradient solver for GPUs
Technique to reduce iteration dependences through strategic sparsification
Evaluation across diverse SPD matrix problems with ILU(0) and ILU(K)
Significant speedups on NVIDIA A100 GPU
limitations: Evaluation limited to symmetric positive definite matrices; unclear how sparsification affects convergence in other problem classes.
primary_theme: GPU-Accelerated Sparse Linear Solvers via Preconditioner Sparsification
